propositions: The Pass-2/Pass-3 LLM judge exhibits self-consistency drift that injects noise into the Pass-2 sub-answer vocabulary, threatening the stability of the new `asserted_capability_confirmed` sub-answer routed over G6/E4/T3 cohort in R5.

Section-order permutation of input plans can flip gate verdicts, with prior research recording 82.5% pairwise verdict flips; residual order-sensitivity must be empirically verified below a floor before R3 lands a new order-exposed container criterion.

E6 re-judges 50 frozen findings from the R5 cohort (G6/E4/T3) three times each to measure self-consistency via Fleiss' κ and raw agreement, with a pass floor of κ≥0.6 AND raw≥0.8; sub-floor results block R5.

E6 shuffles section order on 14 committed plans (≥3 top-level sections from corpus_sample.json) into exactly 3 distinct permutations each and measures verdict stability via the public review_plan entrypoint, with an identical pass floor (κ≥0.6 AND raw≥0.8); sub-floor results block R3.

Infrastructure-level INDETERMINATE verdicts (carrying coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed) are excluded as execution failures and re-runs are attempted, while genuine judge-INDETERMINATE (neither flag set) is retained as a valid agreement category.

Experiment A measures 150 billable LLM calls (50 findings × 3 votes via agentic Pass-2) and Experiment B measures 42 calls (14 plans × 3 permutations via full-gate review), all bounded and non-mutating to the production store.
